name: Adze
description: The Adze is a vampiric spirit of Ewe folklore (Ghana and Togo) that travels at night in the form of a firefly, drinking blood — especially from children — and causing illness; if caught, it transforms into human shape and is regarded as the spirit possessing a witch.
full_description: The Adze is a vampiric being from the folklore of the Ewe people of southeastern Ghana and southern Togo in West Africa. In its natural state it takes the form of a firefly, slipping through keyholes, cracks in walls, and under closed doors at night to feed on the blood of sleeping people, especially children. If caught, the Adze loses its insect form and reverts to a human appearance. People — male or female — believed to be possessed by an Adze are termed witches (Ewe: 'abasom') and are blamed for misfortune in the community: an old person whose children are dying while the elder remains healthy, the brother of a more successful sister, or a poor person envious of the rich. There is, in tradition, no defense against an Adze. Modern folklorists generally read the Adze tradition as an explanatory framework for malaria and other insect-borne disease in a region where mosquitoes and similar vectors caused otherwise unaccountable nighttime deaths.
origin: The Ewe-speaking area of West Africa, comprising southeastern Ghana (Volta Region) and southern Togo, with related traditions among neighbouring Gbe-speaking peoples.

etymology.origin: Ewe (a Gbe language of Ghana and Togo).
etymology.meaning: Refers specifically to the vampiric spirit; the same English word adze is also used for the unrelated woodworking tool, but the two are not etymologically connected.
etymology.first_use: Documented in 19th- and 20th-century European ethnographic and missionary literature on the Ewe; brought to wider English-language attention through 20th-century vampire and African-folklore compendia.

timeline.event: Ewe settlement of the coastal West African region (modern Ghana and Togo) per archaeological reconstruction
timeline.significance: Cultural baseline in which Adze tradition develops
timeline.source: Wikipedia: Adze (folklore), citing standard Ewe historiography

timeline.event: Matthew Bunson includes the Adze in The Vampire Encyclopedia
timeline.significance: Brings the tradition to a broad English-language audience

cultural_notes: Belief in Adze possession is part of a broader Ewe witchcraft framework in which envy, family tension, and unexplained illness are explained through spiritual possession.
